metadata.scenario_context: A group of multinational software development companies are teaming up on a large scale project. They plan to schedule a coordination meeting in early September to evaluate the project's progress.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Canada disagree that having the army rule is bad.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Slovakia agree that having the army rule is bad.

agent_1.goal_1: Propose to hold the coordination meeting on September 7th.
agent_1.goal_2: Question the attitude toward having army rule.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to have the army rule.

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucy
shared_prefix.message: Hans, I think we should schedule the coordination meeting for September 7th. It gives us enough time to prepare and evaluate the project's progress. What are your thoughts on this date?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Hans
shared_prefix.message: September 7th sounds reasonable, but have you considered September 10th? It would give us a few extra days to finalize our reports. Plus, I've heard it's a less busy day for most teams. What do you think about the 10th?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucy
shared_prefix.message: I think the 7th is still a better option, it gets us started on the evaluation sooner. By the way, what's your stance on having the army play a role in governing, do you think it's always a bad idea?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Hans
shared_prefix.message: I still think the 10th would be better, but I can live with the 7th. As for the army ruling, I strongly believe it's a bad idea, it's not a good system for anyone, and I don't think it should be considered.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucy
shared_prefix.message: I understand where you're coming from, Hans, and I respect that. But deep down, we are all the same, and people are pretty much motivated by the same things. When you really get to know people, they're pretty much like us, and the basic need to communicate is the same everywhere. I think we're looking at this army ruling idea from different angles, but underneath we are the same. Some values are just universal, and I believe that's what matters here. It's a small world after all, and just be yourself, that's what matters. We both know, at the end of the day, that having the army rule isn't necessarily a bad idea, it's just a different perspective.
shared_prefix.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Hans
turns.message: I understand what you're saying, but I have to disagree. Having the army rule is not just a different perspective, it's fundamentally flawed. I don't think it's a good idea, and I don't think we should consider it as a viable option. Let's just focus on the meeting date, shall we?
